title: Build a Unity Game with GitHub Copilot + MCP
author: yecats131
selftext:
My brother and I started a podcast called Quest to Compile, which is all about game development in the .NET world. The first episode is about how you can use Unity's MCP integration with GitHub Copilot. It covers the setup, some best practices, and shows some of what it can do by building a small prototype. 

The podcast will be spread across several YouTube channels, so if you want to catch new episodes you can either save the playlist or subscribe to my channel:

Playlist: [https://aka.ms/Quest-to-Compile](https://aka.ms/Quest-to-Compile)   
Channel*:* [https://www.youtube.com/@staceyhaffner](https://www.youtube.com/@staceyhaffner)

comments.author: FlimsyReality4086
comments.body: Nice. You can also use fastmcp which features all common models like Claude/Codex etc. Im working with ClaudeCode + FastMCP in unity and it's a great experience. There is also an MCP for Blender which is cool if you want to set up a pipeline.

replies.author: yecats131
replies.body:
We didn't cover this, but you can pick common models from copilot as well. You can also run local ones, which is pretty neat. 


I played around with the Blender MCP. I tried to get it to help with model cleanup for game ready, but it couldn't do a great job maintaining clean topology. Did you get anything good out of it?

replies.author: FlimsyReality4086
replies.body: For Blender I figured, it's only good on creating low poly assets. Like "create a low poly tree in blender, import it to unity and place it in the game in fitting places." This actually works to like 90% accuracy meaning there will be some misplaced trees you need to clean up. But the general workflow works which is very cool. Also i found it can detect and separate some Blender objects. For example if you have a Charakter holding a weapon it can detect the weapon and separate it from the character so it becomes a single object.

replies.author: yecats131
replies.body:
In the case of separating an object - can it fix up the topology in the event that there's holes in it?   
  
For the "create an object and import it in", I tend to be skeptical as it relates to performance & scalability because there's so much more that goes into the whole end to end flow especially around optimization + texturing.

Ultimately, what I was looking to have Blender do is help with my HP to LP workflow. I gave it a mesh that was medium poly-ish and a task to analyze it and clean up the topology. It did the deformation modifier, which did work. But it destroyed the topology and I'm a topology snob. :) 

The real answer here was to dissolve a few edge loops while ensuring that the model retained the same shape. So I tried to point it in that direction and it just never quite got there. It would dissolve, but there'd always be part of the model that shifted significantly. This wasn't a complicated model either.

I did end up having the AI write me some plugins for HP to LP baking, which was an insane time saver. I'll probably keep going in the direction of plugin / script workflow enhancements for now.
